sources.entry: boto3 - Python interface to Amazon Web Services.

summary.one_liner: Boto3 is the official AWS SDK for Python, letting Python code work with Amazon services such as S3 and EC2.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Python interface to Amazon Web Services so developers can write code that uses AWS services like Amazon S3 and Amazon EC2. The README points to an external doc site listing supported services. Installation is from PyPI with pip, or from source using a cloned repo and an editable install. Credentials are configured through standard AWS files such as ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.aws/config, with other credential methods described in linked docs. A short example shows creating an S3 resource and listing bucket names. The README also covers running unit and functional tests with tox or pytest, and it lists GitHub issues, Stack Overflow, and AWS Support as help channels.
use_cases: access Amazon S3 buckets from Python
control Amazon EC2 instances from scripts
write cloud applications that call AWS APIs
list or manage AWS resources from a Python program
how_to_run: Configure credentials in ~/.aws/credentials and region in ~/.aws/config
python -c "import boto3; s3 = boto3.resource('s3'); [print(b.name) for b in s3.buckets.all()]"
notable: Official AWS SDK for Python, maintained and published by Amazon Web Services
Resource and client interfaces for AWS services such as S3 and EC2
Reads standard AWS shared credentials and config files
Python 3.9 support ended on 2026-04-29 per the README notice
caveats: Python 3.9 support has ended; a supported newer Python version is required
Requires AWS credentials and a default region to be configured before use
The maintainers say they have limited bandwidth to address GitHub issues
